Title: Notify ISACA of the new leaders
Guidebook text: Following the chapter's Annual General Meeting (AGM), or whenever a change in leadership occurs, the outgoing Chapter President should promptly notify the Chapter Experience team through ISACA Support of all newly elected and appointed chapter leaders. This helps ensure chapter records remain accurate and that new leaders receive timely access to chapter resources, communications, systems, and support.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 8 (Immediately Following the Annual General Meeting)

Title: Hand over records and knowledge
Guidebook text: Ensure the timely transfer of relevant chapter records, files, correspondence, credentials, and institutional knowledge to incoming officers, directors, committee chairs, and other authorized leaders.

Title: Close out reporting and compliance
Guidebook text: Confirm that all required annual reporting and compliance obligations have been completed or appropriately assigned, including any reports due to ISACA Global.

Title: Set a handover timeline
Guidebook text: Establish a transition timeline and target completion date for all turnover activities.

Title: Update procedures and records
Guidebook text: Coordinate with chapter officers, directors, and committee chairs to review and update chapter procedures, forms, operational documentation, and governance records, as appropriate.

Title: List the open items
Guidebook text: Prepare, or coordinate the preparation of, a list of open items and ongoing activities requiring follow-up by incoming leaders. Examples may include: Outstanding invoices awaiting payment approval or processing. Venue, facility, or service contracts for upcoming chapter events. Speaker, instructor, sponsor, or vendor agreements for future programs. Strategic initiatives, projects, or operational matters that remain incomplete. Other commitments, obligations, or action items requiring continued attention.

Title: Hold transition meetings
Guidebook text: Facilitate transition meetings between outgoing and incoming leaders to support knowledge transfer, answer questions, and promote continuity. These meetings may be conducted individually or as a group, depending on the chapter's needs.

Title: Review assets with the Treasurer
Guidebook text: Work with the Treasurer to review and update the chapter's inventory of assets, equipment, records, and other chapter property.

Title: Transfer chapter property
Guidebook text: Ensure that all chapter-owned property, records, and resources are appropriately transferred to authorized incoming leaders.

Title: Update bank signers and accounts
Guidebook text: Confirm that banking, financial, and other administrative accounts are updated as necessary to reflect leadership changes, including authorized signatories. Chapters are encouraged to maintain multiple authorized signers and appropriate internal controls in accordance with board-approved policies.

Title: Hand over access to accounts
Guidebook text: Ensure access to chapter mailboxes, post office boxes, technology platforms, websites, social media accounts, cloud storage, email systems, and other chapter resources is transferred to authorized incoming leaders and removed for outgoing leaders, as appropriate.

Title: Pass on correspondence and ISACA guidance
Guidebook text: Transfer current correspondence files and other important records to the incoming Chapter President, including materials, resources, and guidance provided by ISACA Global that may support future chapter operations.

Title: Thank the year's volunteers
Guidebook text: The outgoing Chapter President should also consider coordinating a volunteer Recognition activity or event to acknowledge and celebrate the contributions of board members, committee leaders, volunteers, and members whose efforts supported the chapter's success throughout the year.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 13 (Recognition and Appreciation)
